facts.label: Said + past progressive
facts.sub: Para contar o que alguém estava fazendo, use said + was/were + -ing: They said they were coming. Com pessoa, use told me: She told me she was bringing it.

facts.label: O que estavam fazendo
facts.sub: Use said + sujeito + was ou were + verbo com -ing: They said they were coming. She said she was bringing her dog. Em um relato, are vira were e is vira was.

facts.label: Contar para alguém
facts.sub: Use told + pessoa: They told me they were waiting. Não diga said me. Depois de told, sempre vem me, us, her, him ou them.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: Are coming becomes were coming in reported speech.
“They said they are coming” is the usual form after a past report.
items.why: Usually: They said they were coming.

items.s: We can use told me before the report.
items.why: Yes: They told me they were coming.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: Are coming becomes were coming in reported speech. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
“They said they are coming” is the usual form after a past report. → Falso (Usually: They said they were coming.)
We can use told me before the report. → Verdadeiro (Yes: They told me they were coming.)

pages.title: A street party · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a sunny Saturday afternoon on a quiet street in Portland. People put tables and chairs on the sidewalk. Fay wears a green hat and carries a bag. Her neighbor Paloma waits near a big tree. The street party starts at six. Fay asks who is coming.

“Paloma, are you sure the neighbors are coming to the street party?” says Fay. “Yes, they said they were coming at six with some food.” says Paloma. “And the band? The singer told me they were playing near the corner.” says Fay.

pages.title: Laboratório de sons · o som
pages.what: Were soa “uêr” no inglês americano, curto e fraco. Where soa “uér”, com o som mais aberto e longo.
